results.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Final Results for August 2026 Declines 6% Month-Over-Month, Year-ahead Inflation Expectations at 4.0%. Sentiment Under Trump is Down 11.2% Year-Over-Year and 24% Lower Than Biden in August 2024.

results.content:
The University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index was revised upward to 51.7 in August 2026, from a preliminary reading of 51.0, according to Trading Economics. Despite the revision, sentiment fell about 6% from July and remained roughly 11% below its year-ago level, reflecting persistent concerns that inflation will stay elevated for the foreseeable future. [...] Consumers are increasingly worried about weakening economic conditions. One-year business expectations fell 10%, while the five-year outlook dropped 13%. Meanwhile, one-year inflation expectations eased to 4.0% from 4.2%, and long-run expectations held steady at 3.3% for a third consecutive month.

NEW YORK, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- The U.S. consumer sentiment in August fell about 6 percent from July and about 11 percent from a year ago as inflation concerns persisted, a survey showed Friday.

The Index of Consumer Sentiment released by the University of Michigan (UM) Surveys of Consumers slipped to 51.7 in the August 2026 survey, down from 55.2 in July and below last August's 58.2.
